1.note: The author is using the term **house** by association to mean all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Saul** figuratively means all the people descended from King Saul. (This is slightly different from the uses of this phrase in [chapter 3](ta:03) to mean “the supporters of Saul” or “the successors of Saul.”) Alternate translation: [among the descendants of Saul]

2.note: Here the author is introducing **Ziba** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Now there was a certain servant named Ziba in Saul’s household]

Ziba is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Yes, your servant is Ziba]

Ziba is speaking of himself in the third person as **Your servant** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person. Alternate translation: [Yes, I am Ziba]

Ziba is responding to David with the courteous expression that a person in this culture would use to tell a superior that he had heard a summons and was ready and willing to obey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Yes, I am Ziba, and I am ready to obey you]

3.note: Here the masculine term **a man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [a person] or [anyone]

David is using the possessive form **the covenant faithfulness of God** to mean the covenant faithfulness that he will show to such a person because of the oath he swore to God. He does not mean God’s own covenant faithfulness. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the covenant faithfulness that I swore to God I would do]

4.note: Ziba is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [I will tell you]

6.note: Be sure that it is clear in your translation that Mephibosheth did not fall down accidentally. He knelt down in front of David, pressing his face to the ground and stretching himself out completely, as a gesture to honor David. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action. Alternate translation: [and he knelt down and pressed his face to the ground in front of David, stretching himself out completely, to show David great honor]

Mephibosheth is speaking of himself in the third person as **your servant** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person. Alternate translation: [Behold me]

Mephibosheth is responding to David with the courteous expression that a person in this culture would use to tell a superior that he had heard a summons and was ready and willing to obey. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. The meaning here is the same as for the expression “Behold me” in 1:7. See how you translated that expression there.

7.q: אַל־תִּירָ֗א כִּ֣י עָשֹׂה֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה עִמְּ⁠ךָ֥ חֶ֨סֶד֙ בַּֽ⁠עֲבוּר֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן אָבִ֔י⁠ךָ
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Doing, I will do covenant faithfulness with you for the sake of Jonathan your father, so do not fear]

David is repeating forms of the verb **do** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [I will certainly do]

In this verse, the word **field** is singular in form, but it refers to all of Saul’s agricultural lands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “field.” Alternate translation: [the fields of] or [the lands of]
Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship. Saul was actually the father of the father of Mephibosheth. Alternate translation: [Saul your grandfather]

David is using **bread** to represent food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [food] or [meals]

David is using the term **table** to represent eating meals as part of his household. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with the rest of my household]

8.q: מֶ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑⁠ךָ כִּ֣י פָנִ֔יתָ אֶל־הַ⁠כֶּ֥לֶב הַ⁠מֵּ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֽוֹ⁠נִי
8.note: Mephibosheth is using the question form to express humility and to emphasize that he does not deserve such kindness. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Your servant is not anyone important, that you should turn to a dead dog that is like me!]

Mephibosheth is speaking as if David would physically **turn** toward him. In this context, **turn to** represents “show regard for” or “show kindness to.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that you should show any regard for]

Mephibosheth is speaking as if he were actually a **dead dog**. In this culture, dogs were wild, and they were considered dirty and regarded with contempt. Moreover, a **dead dog** would be powerless. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 24:14. Alternate translation: [someone like me who is powerless and whom people regard with contempt]

9.note: While the author refers to Ziba as a **young man** who belonged to Saul, in this context he is using that term to mean “servant,” which is what he calls Ziba in the rest of this chapter. Since Ziba had many grown sons, he was not physically a “young man.” If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use the term “servant” here. Alternate translation: [the servant of Saul]
See how you translated the similar expression in [9:1](ta:09). Alternate translation: [his family]

Mephibosheth was actually the son of the son of Ziba’s master. Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship that would be appropriate to use here and in the next verse. Alternate translation: [to the grandson of]

10.note: The word **you** is singular here because David is addressing Ziba directly. However, the context makes clear that David is commanding Ziba’s sons and servants to be involved in these actions as well. It may be more appropriate to use a plural form of “you” in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated the similar expression in 9:7. Alternate translation: [food … meals]
See how you translated the similar expression in 9:7.

10.q: וּ⁠לְ⁠צִיבָ֗א חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר בָּנִ֖ים וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדִֽים
10.note: Here, the author is providing background information to help readers understand something that happens later in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

11.q: יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֲדֹנִ֤⁠י הַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת־עַבְדּ֔⁠וֹ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑⁠ךָ
11.note: Ziba is speaking about David respectfully and about himself humbly in the third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate his reference to David in the second person and his reference to himself in the first person. Alternate translation: [you, my lord the king, command me, your servant, thus shall I do]

Ziba is using a verb form that describes action in the present. The implication is that he will do not just what David has commanded him on this occasion but also anything further that David might command him in the future regarding Mephibosheth. Use an appropriate verb form in your language to convey this sense.

The author is quoting David’s words directly, perhaps to show that his command was carried out. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [at his table]

12.note: Here, **the dwelling of the house** means the people who lived in Ziba’s house, that is, the members of his household. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the members of the household of]

13.q: וּ⁠מְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת יֹשֵׁב֙ בִּ⁠יר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י עַל־שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַ⁠מֶּ֛לֶךְ תָּמִ֖יד ה֣וּא אֹכֵ֑ל
13.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [But since Mephibosheth was continually eating at the table of the king, he dwelled in Jerusalem]

Here, the author is providing background information to help readers understand something that happens later in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.
